Today, our capabilities span MEICA, EICAT, civil engineering, control-panel design and manufacture, automation, software and digital transformation. You'll also work directly with clients and commercial stakeholders, keeping everyone aligned, resolving issues proactively and ensuring projects meet specification, timescale and commercial objectives. It's a varied role requiring someone who can see the bigger picture while staying close enough to the detail to keep projects moving. Lead Clients, Stakeholders & Safety • Attend Client Progress Team meetings and build strong relationships with clients, stakeholders and commercial leads. • Maintain excellent HSE standards across project sites and lead by example on safety behaviours. • Ensure projects operate in line with relevant legislation and CDM requirements. • Communicate project challenges, changes and risks clearly and proactively. About You You'll bring proven experience delivering civil engineering projects within utilities or infrastructure and understand the practical, technical and commercial demands involved. You'll be comfortable coordinating multiple projects and stakeholders, managing changing priorities and making confident decisions when challenges arise. Most importantly, you'll be someone who takes ownership of delivery rather than simply reporting on it. You'll Bring: • Proven civil project delivery experience within utilities and/or infrastructure. • Strong knowledge of civil engineering and construction methods. • Experience managing complex programmes, budgets and resources. • Confidence managing project teams, subcontractors and suppliers. • Strong commercial awareness, including costs, variations and project risk. • Excellent knowledge of Health & Safety legislation and CDM regulations. • Strong client and stakeholder management capability. • Excellent leadership, communication and practical problem-solving skills. • Proficiency with project management and reporting tools. • A collaborative and proactive approach. • Full UK driving licence. Why CHG Electrical? You'll be joining a growing engineering organisation where you'll have genuine responsibility for delivery and the opportunity to influence how projects are run. You'll work across varied utilities and infrastructure projects, collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams and continue developing your expertise as the business grows. You'll Also Receive: • £50,000 - £60,000 salary DOE. • Car allowance and fuel card. • Performance-based bonus scheme. • 25 days' annual leave plus 8 bank holidays. • Flexible working arrangements. • Ongoing training and development. • Clear opportunities for career progression. review_candidates.description: Role: Director of Operations Location: Remote-first with quarterly travel to Ireland, plus occasional client site visits across the UK Compensation: From £100,000 onwards (flexible depending on candidate experience) About the Role We are working with a fast-growing health technology company whose product is helping NHS trusts and health systems improve patient care. As the business is expanding across the UK, Ireland, and Europe, they are looking for a VP of Operations & Technical Delivery to lead the entire customer journey after a sale is agreed. This is a senior, hands-on leadership role. You will oversee day-to-day project delivery, manage Trust implementations, and build the operational processes needed to help the company grow. You should be equally comfortable presenting delivery updates to the board and working directly with NHS IT teams to solve technical interface issues on go-live day. Key Responsibilities Customer Delivery Lifecycle: Own projects from the point of contract handover through project kick-off, technical build, go-live, and post-launch support. NHS Technical Implementations: Lead solution design and technical delivery for key NHS hospital deployments. Hospital System Integration: Work hands-on with NHS integration teams across EPR, PAS, RIS, and LIMS systems, using standard healthcare interfaces including HL7, FHIR, and MESH. Go-Live Management: Lead cutover planning, CAB approvals, and go/no-go calls, ensuring hazard logs and clinical safety sign-offs are in place before launch. Supplier Coordination: Manage relationships and technical dependencies with third-party healthcare software vendors. Operational Process & Governance: Build repeatable implementation steps, manage team capacity, monitor operational budgets, and ensure delivery meets ISO 13485, ISO 27001, and DTAC requirements. Team Leadership: Manage and mentor the implementation and support teams, planning recruitment as the customer base expands. What We Are Looking For Healthcare & NHS Experience: A proven track record delivering software or SaaS products into NHS trusts and healthcare providers. Technical Integration Skills: Solid, practical understanding of healthcare integrations, specifically HL7 interfaces alongside core systems like EPR, PAS, RIS, or pathology platforms. Clinical Safety & Governance Awareness: Experience working within formal clinical safety standards (DCB0129 / DCB0160) and quality management systems. Leadership & Delivery Ownership: Prior experience leading professional services, implementation, or operations teams in a healthcare software business. Pragmatic, Problem-Solving Approach: Someone who takes direct ownership of customer issues, communicates well with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and thrives in a growing company. What Is on Offer A key leadership position working closely with the CEO and founders. Direct influence over the company's delivery model and international growth. A clear progression route to Chief Operating Officer (COO) as the team and business scale. Flexible, remote-first working with travel for key customer milestones.
